claims.text: The applicable starting material is equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi in a single-phase solid-solution state.
Equimolar CoCrFeNiTi has relatively low hardness and strength.
Equimolar CoCrFeNiTi has favorable plasticity and machinability.
Minimal lattice distortion primarily governs the alloy's low hardness and strength.
The equimolar composition produces only modest atomic-size differences among its constituents.
Limited lattice distortion provides only weak solid-solution strengthening.
Limited lattice distortion permits comparatively easy dislocation glide.
Easy dislocation glide promotes dynamic recovery during deformation.
Dynamic recovery limits the accumulation of dislocation density.
Limited dislocation accumulation reduces strain hardening.
Plastic deformation occurs predominantly through dislocation slip with rapid recovery.
Relative to an enhanced-lattice-distortion composition, the equimolar alloy should yield earlier and have lower yield strength.
Relative to an enhanced-lattice-distortion composition, the equimolar alloy should exhibit less strain hardening.
Relative to an enhanced-lattice-distortion composition, the equimolar alloy should retain a lower dislocation density during deformation.
An off-equimolar variant with increased lattice distortion should exhibit greater strain hardening.
An off-equimolar variant with increased lattice distortion should exhibit higher hardness.
The proposed mechanism is restricted to single-phase solid solutions under quasi-static loading at temperatures that do not cause phase transformation or precipitation.
Local compositional fluctuations or atomic clustering could alter dislocation behavior.

contradictions.description: The boundary excludes phase transformation and precipitation, but the falsification rule treats strengthening from secondary-phase formation as evidence that falsifies the hypothesis. Secondary-phase formation would instead place the test outside the hypothesis's stated domain unless separately designated as a boundary-failure control.
